status: Normative contract for the complete find_uuids candidate; production integration and Cargo qualification are separate gates.

entry.signature: u64 codex_hia_uuid_find(const u8* source, u64 source_len, u8* output, u64 output_capacity, u8* workspace, u64 workspace_len)
entry.status_encoding: Core u32 is zero extended to u64 by the fixed native buffer wrapper.

source_identity.notice: These are immutable preimage identities, not a claim about a future integrated tree.

semantics.search: Scan candidate byte positions in increasing order. A match emits its original [start,end) and resumes at end; a nonmatch advances by one byte. Return every selected match in encounter order.
no_other_constraints: No UUID version or variant check.
semantics.raw_input: Arbitrary bytes are accepted. This is an ASCII byte-pattern matcher, not a UTF-8 validator. In a valid Rust &str, non-ASCII bytes cannot satisfy the pattern, so every match is on UTF-8 boundaries and agrees with the complete regex-lite iterator.
semantics.ownership: HIA borrows source synchronously and emits offsets. Rust copies the selected substrings to independent owned String values.
semantics.source_size: No fixed total source-length limit. Every readable slice length representable by the ABI is supported subject to actual host memory and final output allocation.

caller_preconditions: All advertised ranges must be live, readable for source/workspace, and writable for output for the synchronous call. Zero-length ranges need not be dereferenced.
The ranges do not overlap. Source and workspace do not change during the call.
Advertised lengths are actual allocated capacities; dangling pointers, aliasing, concurrent mutation, or invented oversized capacities are outside the ABI contract.
Native retains no pointers and has no mutable global state.

operations.name: query
operations.effect: Scan the complete source and write only the 64-byte header. Bytes after the header remain unchanged regardless of capacity.

operations.name: emit
operations.effect: First scan counts matches without stores. Compute and check the full required capacity. Only then rescan and write all selected rows and the header.

fields.name: required_output_bytes
fields.value: 64 + 16 * match_count, for emit regardless of requested operation.

rows.name: end
rows.type: u64 exclusive byte offset into source

row_invariants: Each row selects the original exact bytes; duplicate strings can appear in different rows.
output.success_writes: Exactly [0,written_bytes) may be modified. Output bytes at or beyond written_bytes remain unchanged.

statuses.name: SHORT
statuses.meaning: Workspace shorter than 32, output shorter than 64, or emit output shorter than the final required bytes.

statuses.name: INVALID
statuses.meaning: Workspace length is not exactly 32 after the minimum check; revision, operation or reserved fields invalid; or required-size arithmetic cannot be represented.

precedence: 1. If workspace_len < 32 or output_capacity < 64, return SHORT before any frame read.
3. Validate revision=1, operation in {0,1}, both reserved words=0; otherwise INVALID.
4. Count matches in source without modifying any buffer. Check count <= (u64::MAX - 64) / 16, otherwise INVALID.
5. Compute required = 64 + count * 16. Query requires only its already-checked 64 bytes. Emit returns SHORT if output_capacity < required.
6. All returned failures precede all stores. A valid emit rescans the immutable source, then publishes its header; no error branch remains after any store.

error_atomicity.output: Entire advertised buffer unchanged on every nonzero return, including tail bytes beyond a nominal header or an insufficient partial row table.
error_atomicity.outside_advertised_buffers: Never accessed by any valid call.
error_atomicity.semantic_errors: There are no regex syntax or other semantic-error outcomes: the pattern is fixed and native matching accepts every source byte sequence.

arithmetic_invariants: Lengths and offsets use unsigned 64-bit usize on the pinned target. For n < 36 scan returns zero without any source load.
Otherwise limit = n - 36 is guarded. A candidate index i <= limit implies i + 36 <= n; all fixed-offset loads are below n.
Mismatch advances i + 1 <= n - 35; match advances i + 36 <= n. Every iteration advances strictly, so scans terminate.
Matches are disjoint intervals of 36 bytes, so count <= floor(n / 36) and count increments cannot overflow.

The explicit guard count <= floor((u64::MAX - 64) / 16) precedes multiplication and header addition. The sharper disjointness bound also implies representability for every representable source length.

During emission, row index k is smaller than the previously counted total. Offset 64 + 16*k and the two u64 stores lie within required. Immutable input makes count-only and emit rescans select the same intervals.
Source offset usize-to-u64 casts preserve all bits on the fixed target. The Rust adapter rejects unrepresentable words and malformed output plans rather than falling back.

hia: Full scan and earliest candidate selection.
Required capacity and byte span plan.
rust: Own/borrow input and allocate query/table/result buffers.
Validate status, header consistency, ordered fixed-width in-bounds UTF-8 slices.
implementation_boundary.fallback: None in the native feature path. The original complete Rust function remains byte-preserved under cfg(not(feature="hia-native")) until a later separately authorized retirement.
